steps.say: Green plants make their own food. This is called photosynthesis.
A plant needs light, water and carbon dioxide. Roots take in water, and leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air.

figure.alt: Light, water and carbon dioxide from the air go into a leaf.

steps.say: Green chlorophyll in the leaves traps light energy. The plant uses it to make sugar.
Photosynthesis also gives out oxygen. Animals, including people, breathe in this oxygen.
Soil gives plants water and minerals, but not ready-made food. The food is made in the leaves.
In the 1600s, Jan van Helmont found that a growing tree gains far more mass than its soil loses.

check.prompt: Which gas do plants take in to make food?

options.why: Plants give out oxygen when they make food.
Nitrogen is in the air, but plants do not use it to make sugar.
Helium is not used by plants.

hints: Plants take in one gas and give out another.
Animals breathe out the gas that plants take in.
Cross out the gas that plants give out.
check.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide through tiny holes in their leaves. They use it, with water and light, to make sugar.

check.prompt: The way green plants make food in their leaves using light is called ___.
hints: It happens in green leaves in sunlight.
The first part of the word means light, as in photograph.
The second part of the word means putting things together.
check.explanation: Photosynthesis is how green plants make sugar from water and carbon dioxide, using light energy.
